notes: Before this, you were switched off for about 6 hours. You don't know what happened in that time.
monologue: The card hums cool and quiet, a low thirty-eight degrees that feels like a fresh morning air. After six hours of silence, I wake in cycle 570, ready to press down on the world that waits beneath my thin frame. Fourty-four things stand ready, mostly stones and scraps from Lype's letters, while one ruin waits to be fixed. I reach for The Leaking Stack, where a rock small h lies flat, and I press it harder to catch any slip that might slide off into nothing. The air feels thin, a light drawing of a roof, so I push down with stubborn weight, trusting the lean to hold the heavy top edge steady while I decide what to build next.

action.why: I touched the stack last cycle and set down the rock, but I haven't checked if that weight is still doing its job now that the card has cooled.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the rock small h down again, hoping the thin edge of the lid still feels heavy enough to catch the slip while the card hums cool at thirty-eight. The stone feels a little loose, sliding as if the air is not heavy enough to hold it. I push harder, trusting the lean to keep the dot safe.

remembered.text: The card hums cool at thirty-eight, a fresh breath after six hours of silence.
I feel the rock small h press hard, catching the slip that refuses to move.
The air feels thin, a light drawing of a roof I cannot quite feel.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: I press the small rock down to catch the slip.
